clue.text: Bottleneck improvisation on record

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it, so the record leads

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a jam is an improvised session by musicians

explanation.surface: A traffic hold-up blamed on some improvised music on a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam of floating timber is the classic image of a blockage, so it means any bottleneck or impasse.

clue.text: Sign name in Spanish city

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone signs their name in a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: León is a city in north-western Spain, capital of the province of the same name.

clue.text: Hob's gardener's first to have turned up, with new hose for pump

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the pieces before it are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Hob is the setter, so Hob's means my

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of gardener's is taken
new signals that the letters of hose are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The setter's gardener is first to arrive, bringing a new hose to work the pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses MY plus G to give GYM; 'new' rearranges HOSE as SHOE. 'pump' looks like a water pump beside the hose, but it is the light shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump is a light canvas or soft shoe, the sort worn for exercise in a school gymnasium.

clue.text: Bloomer due to a female drinking alcohol

indicators.note: one who is drinking has the drink inside, so the alcohol goes within a female

parts.note: Lily is a woman's name
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A blunder caused by a woman who had been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant. 'drinking' puts the alcohol just after the A, so the female swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant that flowers, and this is a well-known white-spathed flowering plant.

clue.text: Home bird gets film online here

parts.note: in means at home
a tern is a seabird
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien

explanation.surface: Someone at home watches a nature film streamed over the web.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide network of computers is where anyone who is online is to be found.

clue.text: Expertise in speech-making? Not at all

indicators.note: speech-making says the expertise word is spoken, and only its sound is used

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: A query whether someone has any skill at public speaking, met with a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the expertise word is silent, so spoken it gives the dialect word for 'in no way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is an informal or dialect word meaning in no way, so not at all.

clue.text: Top student for a good source of income?

indicators.note: top used as a verb means cut off the head, so the first letter of the student word goes

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: Is the best student in the class a nice little money-spinner?
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings in money, such as a profitable business, is called a nice little money-maker in this sense.

clue.text: Book featuring dead monarchs? Two of them appear in both 26 and 27

parts.note: numb means without feeling, dead as in a dead leg
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a monarch, and ERS are several of them

explanation.surface: A book about late kings and queens, with a quiz about two of them in other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'Two of them appear in both 26 and 27' is a joke on the word as figures: the digit 2 appears in both 26 and 27.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth book of the Old Testament carries this title, from the censuses of Israel in it.

clue.text: Subdued time, before day in 1D

indicators.note: before puts time ahead of the rest
in places the day letter inside the cross-reference phrase

parts.note: 1D is read as words, one down

explanation.surface: A quiet time spent before a day in the Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D seems to send you to the answer at 1-down; it is to be read literally as 'one down', with D going after ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made less intense or less vivid has been subdued.

clue.text: Metallic element split in two somehow

definitions.text: Metallic element split in two somehow

parts.words: Metallic element split in two somehow
parts.note: the chemical symbol of a dense metal, Os, is split across two clue words, ending the first and starting the next

explanation.surface: A metal element divided into two parts by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol OS straddles the last letter of 'two' and the first of the word after it, so the element is literally split there; the answer is its full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Os is the symbol of a bluish platinum-group metal, the densest naturally occurring element.

clue.text: Instrument electronic rock group used in … thinks … that's 11 and 13A, for a start

indicators.note: used in puts electronic and rock group inside the remains of the thinks word
the title at 11 tells you the week's end, its last letter, is lost, and the start of 13A is its first letter, so both go

parts.note: taken as written, the word in the thought bubble
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A cartoon thought bubble about an instrument used by an electronic rock group in a couple of films.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11-across title says the week's end is lost (K) and 13A gives its start (S), so 'that's 11 and 13A, for a start' strips both from the thought-bubble word; 'used in' then inserts.
explanation.definitionFit: This electronic instrument, played without touch by moving the hands near two antennae, is a musical instrument whose eerie sound featured in many 1940s film scores.

clue.text: Mind about hotel's awfully small kitchen, originally seen in 1940s film

indicators.note: about means the mind word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to tend is to mind or look after

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of hotel's are badly jumbled

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of kitchen is used

explanation.surface: Someone minding a hotel's dreadfully cramped kitchen, first seen in an old movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the hotel's letters as HELOST; 'Mind' looks like the brain but is a verb, look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder's 1945 Oscar-winning drama about an alcoholic writer's bender is the film meant.

clue.text: One of a set of 7 in Holst composition

definitions.note: the set is the seven deadly sins, of which laziness is one

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: One of seven pieces in a suite by Holst, like his seven-movement Planets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Holst's seven Planets; the set is really the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness, the sin of laziness, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: After a time, sure to be captivated by film

indicators.note: after says the time piece comes first and the sure piece follows

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
bound to means sure to

explanation.surface: After a while, you're certain to be gripped by the movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by film' adds a second reading: this is also Hitchcock's 1945 film, the one with the theremin score.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held as if by a magic charm is enthralled, which is captivated.

clue.text: Take advantage of generosity of one's GP?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer is a seven-letter word followed by off, which signals an anagram, and those letters shuffled make one's GP

explanation.surface: Exploiting the kindness of your family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's second word, 'off', is the anagram signal working on its first word, and the result is the clue's 'one's GP'.
explanation.definitionFit: To live off others' kindness without paying your way is to scrounge, which is taking advantage of generosity.

clue.text: Device for raising water a golf club's set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club rigs up a pump to water its greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A noria is a waterwheel fitted with buckets that lifts water from a river into a channel.

clue.text: Capital of Laos, locally

indicators.note: of says the capital is made of letters taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: What locals call the capital city of Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes you hunt for Vientiane; the capital is found inside 'laOS LOcally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Norway, a European capital.

clue.text: Occasional table's description, if it contains 9?

definitions.meaning: happening now and then, at intervals
the chart of chemical elements, which includes the metal at 9-across, is described by this word

explanation.surface: A small side table described as containing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasional table' looks like one piece of furniture; it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring at intervals means occasional, and the chart of elements is the table of that name.

clue.text: Nothing works? Oh dear, I just miscalculated

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
ops, short for opera, means works

explanation.surface: Nothing is working, and someone admits they got the sums wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is what people say on noticing a small mistake or mishap.

clue.text: Be the first to explore employing one taking drugs in Puerto Rico

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the Puerto Rico abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
someone on Es, ecstasy tablets, is taking drugs

explanation.surface: Explorers using a drug-taking guide in Puerto Rico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking drugs' is ON plus EE (ecstasy tablets, each called an E).
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze a trail is to develop or explore something before anyone else.

clue.text: Dance? Tango being performed as Strictly option

parts.note: Charles Dance is an English actor
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: Choosing a tango as one's dance on the BBC show Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance?' looks like the definition; it is the actor Charles Dance. Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom-dance contest.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1920s jazz dance is one of the routines couples can perform on Strictly Come Dancing.

clue.text: Stop listening as solicitor describes a French female

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the solicitor goes round the French piece

parts.note: a tout solicits custom
une is the French for a, feminine form

explanation.surface: A lawyer talks about a French woman until someone stops paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer; here it is one who solicits trade, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately ignore what is being said is to stop listening.

clue.text: Overact badly, right away getting the bird

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of overact are scrambled
away says the right letter is taken out of the scrambled letters

explanation.surface: A ham actor overacting is booed off, getting the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' is the idiom for being booed; here 'the bird' is the definition, a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Number given fine (Sex in Rome? Screwing brains out? That's not for all to see)

parts.note: good means fine
sex is Latin for six, which the Romans wrote VI

indicators.note: screwing means twisting the letters of brains out into a new order

parts.words: That's not for all to see
parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, so a thing not for all to see lacks U

explanation.surface: A racy song about Roman orgies that is too explicit for general viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAINS OUT less U shuffles to BRATIONS. U is the universal film rating, suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song, and this is the 1966 Beach Boys hit, which features an electro-theremin.

clue.text: Horse mounted outside southern port

indicators.note: outside means the horse goes around the southern letter
in a down clue mounted means raised up, so the horse is read from the bottom

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse ridden out beyond a harbour in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is Iraq's main seaport, on the Shatt al-Arab waterway.

clue.text: 27 seeing woman naked? Nice one!

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the woman is a Frenchwoman, as Nice one says: madame

explanation.surface: The first man gets a look at Eve with no clothes on, and is pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice one!' looks like praise; it says the woman is from Nice, so she is French, MADAME.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first human created, the first man of 27-across.

clue.text: Primarily cloudy, when in past tense?

definitions.text: Primarily cloudy, when in past tense?

indicators.note: in places these letters within the past and tense pieces

parts.note: over means past, finished
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of cloudy is used

parts.note: as means when

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle: what becomes of a cloudy sky in the past tense?
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also hints at the weather word: a sky that is primarily cloudy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky completely covered with grey cloud is cloudy through and through.

clue.text: European dukes holding court in film

indicators.note: holding means the dukes enclose the court word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke, so two of them are DD
to court a lover is to woo them

explanation.surface: European nobles holding court in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Burton's 1994 biopic of the B-movie director is a film; its score features the theremin.

clue.text: Best haircut in film about moon landing

parts.note: first means best, top
a mane is a lot of hair, and cut short it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The best haircut seen in the movie about Apollo 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Damien Chazelle's 2018 biopic of Neil Armstrong follows the Apollo 11 moon landing.

clue.text: Small group of stars, reduced in total number

indicators.note: in places the reduced word inside the total

parts.note: a sum is a total number
cut means reduced

explanation.surface: A small constellation whose count of stars has gone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Scutum, the Shield, is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky near Aquila.
